titel: [Ep. 350] Embodied Parenting: Teens, Single Parenting, and Sleep Deprivation

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Somatic parenting strategies for teens, single parents, and sleep deprivation.
kurzfassung: Luis Mojica addresses listener questions about parenting through a somatic lens, focusing on nervous system capacity and co-regulation. He explains how sleep deprivation depletes parental patience and offers non-verbal ways to help children sleep. Furthermore, he discusses managing single parenting, teenage disconnection, meltdowns, and sibling rivalry.
stichpunkte: Somatic therapist Luis Mojica hosts a Q&A session about his upcoming Embodied Parenting group program
Parental capacity determines connection quality, and sleep deprivation directly shrinks that physiological capacity
Traditional sleep training that relies on prolonged crying can push a child into a freeze response
Non-verbal co-regulation, such as quiet presence and gentle touch, helps children settle without over-activating them
Single parents and those with chronically ill partners carry a load meant for multiple bodies, making rest vital
Teenage withdrawal is often driven by technology overload rather than personal rejection from the child
Parallel activities like walking or watching a movie together create safe connection points with distant teens
Allowing children to experience meltdowns without matching their panic teaches them emotional anchoring

kapitel.titel: Navigating Late Teens and Young Adults

beschreibung:
Luis gives us question-and-answer style examples of his upcoming six month Embodied Parenting Slow Group, starting October 6th.
https://www.holisticlifenavigation.com/parenting-group

Parents ask how to single parent, or co-parent with a sick partner, how to parent while sleep deprived without doing the "cry it out" method, and how to parent rebellious teens and siblings. And a big one: how do you regulate once in crisis mode?
Capacity is key! Luis discusses nuances of each topic, and he gives a pendulation practice to help build capacity. Balancing foods are also paramount in helping support our nervous systems to have capacity.
